summary_out.hypothesis: I expected the disjunction to add skips strictly on top of base's skip set (skip iff base OR ratio-with-busy-floor adverse), with admitted-trades strictly <= base by construction, and pnl > base under the loop-1-established '$47 per 1k extra skips' rule. The data shows the ratio leg never fires on any order beyond what base already skips: whenever |net_flow| < 2.0 (absolute leg silent) and abs_vol >= 5.0 (busyness floor met), the ratio |net_flow|/abs_vol is structurally < 0.35 (since |net_flow| < 2.0 / 5.0 = 0.4 already; at abs_vol >= ~5.7, |net_flow|=1 or 1.5 gives |r| < 0.35). The disjunction collapsed to base because flow=2, ratio=0.35, busy_floor=5 makes the ratio leg structurally dominated by the absolute leg on this oracle.
summary_out.brief_summary: afg-b-l3 (aggressor-flow-gate brief-summary loop 3) replaced L2's CONJUNCTION with a DISJUNCTION: skip iff (|net_flow| >= 2.0) OR (|r| >= 0.35 AND abs_vol >= 5.0). Result: PASS vs simple (+2142.77% pnl, +5.0% gate cleared by wide margin) but EXACTLY IDENTICAL to base on the same 11 dates (pnl=$970.00=base, trades=87,760=base, 0 differences). The ratio leg with busyness floor (5 contracts) is structurally dominated by the absolute leg (2 contracts): for any order where |net_flow|<2 and abs_vol>=5, the ratio |net_flow|/abs_vol is mechanically <0.35 too. The L1+L2+L3 trio collectively triangulate: the ratio reformulation cannot beat base on this oracle no matter how it is composed -- it is RELAXED in pure form (L1), STRICTLY-RELAXED-UNION in conjunction (L2), and STRUCTURALLY-INERT in disjunction with the chosen busy_floor (L3). To beat base, the next change must instead modify the base's absolute threshold itself or attack an orthogonal axis (window length / per-side thresholds / regime gates).
summary_out.next: Tighten the base's absolute threshold directly: flow_threshold 2.0 -> 3.0 contracts (single-parameter monotone change, drop the ratio leg entirely to isolate the absolute-threshold effect). L1+L2+L3 collectively suggest the base under-skips on this oracle (extra skips beyond base are weakly anti-informative per L1's $47/1k arithmetic), and the most direct way to ADD skips on top of base's set is to raise its own threshold. Expected direction: trade_count drops by O(5-15%) (low-magnitude absolute-imbalance orders now skipped), pnl > base if those orders are weakly anti-informative on average. If pnl regresses, the L1 '$47/1k' rule was an artefact of the particular ratio-gate-admitted-orders distribution rather than a general property of base's near-margin admits, and L5 should pivot structurally (window length / per-side asymmetric thresholds / session-time regime gates). Avoid: any further ratio-based variants (L1+L2+L3 have exhausted the ratio axis on this oracle); raising busy_floor (the structural dominance argument shows it would only collapse to base faster); CONJUNCTIVE constructions (L2 already established the union-of-admits trap).
